problem: Multi-object navigation methods with persistent semantic memory (e.g., OneMap) use planar 2D maps and cannot handle stairs or vertically overlapping spaces, while cross-floor ObjectNav methods handle only a single goal and keep no reusable queryable semantic memory.
motivation: Real indoor agents must search for several objects in sequence and move between floors. A unified solution needs both vertical traversability and semantic memory that persists across goals. No benchmark existed for sequential multi-object navigation requiring floor transitions.
key_idea: Maintain one sparse 3D voxel map that stores support-aware traversability, stair structure, and goal-independent dense CLIP-aligned features, re-query it for each new goal to produce History POIs, and drive a unified frontier/stair/POI policy with mode-aware 3D A*.
insight: Explicit stair representation is what makes cross-floor sequences solvable: on the Cross-Floor-Required subset, OneMap gets 0.00 SR while LifelongCrossNav gets 7.99. Removing History POIs (w/o H-POI) keeps SR about the same but lowers SPL and PPL, and later-stage conditional SPL stays flat instead of rising. So the efficiency gain on later goals comes from re-querying stored semantics, not from geometry alone. History POIs also raise bed misdetections, so target verification is the main remaining error source.
method: Support-aware sparse 3D voxel map: back-projects RGB-D into 0.1 m voxels, ray-casts free space, and searches downward for support to label Occupied, Traversable, Stair, and Unsupported (fake) voxels.
Stair perception: SegFormer-B2 stair masks lifted to 3D and verified by height variation, step trend, continuity, and support. Stair voxels are promoted only after entering Stair Explore (StairSem).
Persistent 3D semantic memory: SED dense features (24x24x768) are upsampled, lifted to surface voxels, and fused by quality-weighted cumulative averaging across frames and goals.
Query-conditioned retrieval: the new goal's text embedding is compared with voxel features by cosine similarity. High-response regions are clustered and the Top-4 become History POIs.

Unified policy: candidates are Live/History POIs > Traversable > Descend > Ascent frontiers, plus direction-aware Stair Frontiers. An active stair session holds control. Live POIs come from YOLOv7 (YOLO-World for out-of-set queries) with MobileSAM.

Type-aware 3D A*: 26-neighbor graph with voxel-type penalties, and a 1.0 m spherical-neighborhood graph in StairSem. Target approach is checked by a verification step (confidence, mask, visibility, viewing direction, distance).
HM3D-MFMON benchmark and post-hoc stage-wise shortest-path protocol: reference distance is recomputed from the agent's actual stage start, with conditional and global SR/SPL, PR, and PPL.

setting.backbone: Modular pipeline of frozen pretrained models: SED (CLIP-based dense features), SegFormer-B2, YOLOv7, YOLO-World, MobileSAM, plus hand-designed 3D A* planner
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D (640x640, 90° HFOV) plus 6-DoF camera pose
setting.action_space: discrete: MoveForward 0.25 m, TurnLeft/Right 30°, LookUp/Down 30°, Stop
setting.privileged: none (uses ground-truth 6-DoF pose from the simulator)

numbers.extra: 1200-action budget per episode, success radius 1.5 m

results: On all 927 HM3D-MFMON episodes LifelongCrossNav reaches SR 29.13 and SPL 9.64 against OneMap's 16.83 and 6.95. On the CFR subset OneMap has 0.00 SR versus 7.99. On single-object HM3D ObjectNav it gets SR 59.7 and SPL 28.0, below ASCENT (65.4 SR) and OneMap (37.4 SPL).
limitations: Sequence success remains low (29% overall, 8% on CFR), and false target detections (e.g., bed confused with sofa via YOLOv7) are the main failure source.
Evaluated only in simulation on HM3D with six categories and three goals per episode. The only multi-object baseline is OneMap, and ground-truth pose is used.
Single-object SPL is lower than OneMap and ASCENT because the policy explores the current floor before trying cross-floor candidates.
